 Match Preview Como 1907 Cagliari 
 Article Content
 Football
 Football Match Preview | Como 1907-Cagliari Serie A returns to the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia following the international break, with Como 1907 back in action in front of their home supporters twenty days after their last outing in Como. Visiting the Lariani are Cagliari, one of the early-season surprises of the campaign, currently sitting ninth in the table. Kick-off is scheduled for Saturday, 21 November at 3:00 PM.
 Cesc Fàbregas welcomed back twelve Biancoblù players from international duty over the course of the week. Captain Lucas Da Cunha and his teammates are fully focused on Fabio Pisacane’s Sardinian side - the opening test in a demanding run of four consecutive home fixtures in the space of twelve days for the Lariani.
 Cagliari arrive on the shores of Lake Como buoyed by five wins in their opening eleven league matches, including a victory over Frosinone right before the break. The Rossoblù have actually collected the bulk of their points away from Sardinia, claiming maximum points on tough road trips to Parma, Atalanta, and Udinese.
 The Biancoblù are bracing for a compact, disciplined, and brave opponent riding a wave of strong form and performances. However, Fàbregas’ men are equally determined to solidify their own standing near the top end of the table, targeting an eighth league win to build fresh momentum ahead of a packed home schedule.
 The words of Como 1907 head coach Cesc Fàbregas ahead of Como 1907-Cagliari: 
 "Cagliari have a very specific style of play. The statistics also reflect that. They're a team that defend extremely well, with their players staying close together and leaving very little space between the lines.
 Playing at home is obviously important to us. We want to make the most of that advantage by playing in front of our own supporters, avoiding unnecessary travel and having more time to rest and recover.
 Fabio and I have a very good relationship built on mutual respect. I have a great deal of respect for Fabio and what he's doing. He's shown real courage in giving young players opportunities and helping them develop. That's something I admire from him".
 Cagliari 
 Now in their fourth consecutive Serie A campaign—and their second under Pisacane’s guidance—Cagliari are proving they belong in the top flight, backing up their table position with genuinely impressive football.
 Regardless of the shape they deploy, Cagliari present a compact, well-drilled defensive unit while placing a much stronger emphasis on playing out from the back than in recent years. Pisacane’s go-to system is a 4-3-2-1, though he frequently adjusts his tactical setup depending on the opponent or the flow of the match.
 Sitting ninth in the standings, Cagliari also boast the league’s ninth-best defensive record, underscoring the solid organization shielding goalkeeper Elia Caprile. The Rossoblù excel at keeping the lines tight between their units, packing the midfield to deny opponents space before choosing whether to keep the ball or spring vertical counter-attacks.
 Veteran Yerry Mina provides grit and leadership at the heart of the Sardinian backline, flanked by reliable regulars Zé Pedro and Juan Rodríguez—both of whom have started every single one of the opening eleven matchdays. In midfield, Harry Winks and Alessandro Romano - recently called up to the senior Italy squad - dictate the tempo, alongside long-serving club captain Alessandro Deiola.
 Operating between the lines in attacking midfield are Michel Adopo, Jacopo Fazzini, and familiar face Alieu Fadera, who made 28 appearances for the Biancoblù during the 2024/25 season. Up front, Daniel Maldini serves as the main focal point - having already netted five goals this term - though Pisacane can also call upon the likes of Alexandre Mendy, M’Bala Nzola, Kevin Carlos, and Noha Trepy to trouble opposing defenses.
 Head-to-head 
 Como 1907 and Cagliari have met 53 times across all competitions, including 10 encounters in Serie A. In top-flight meetings, the Biancoblù have won half (5), while the Sardinians have prevailed twice alongside three draws.
 Looking specifically at clashes at the Sinigaglia over the past two seasons, Cagliari escaped with a goalless draw in November 2025. Earlier that year, in May on the third-to-last matchday of the 2024/25 season, Fàbregas’ side ran out 3–1 comeback winners thanks to goals from Maxence Caqueret, Gabriel Strefezza, and Patrick Cutrone after Adopo had fired the visitors ahead.
